The '''OI-CT'''<ref name="YouTube">{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Surface Vehicle in Star Wars Movies|video=k7dVRY2QRV0|nolive=1}}</ref> was a quadrupedal<ref name="Solo" /> model of industrial [[crane transport]] [[walker]] manufactured by [[Kuat Drive Yards]]<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" /> and utilized by both the [[Galactic Empire]]<ref name="Dark Lord 23" /> and [[New Republic]].<ref name="Mando">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:OI-CT-Ferrix.png|thumb|left|300px|OI-CTs on Ferrix]]
OI-CTs were massive mobile crane walkers deployed across various industrial worlds that fell within Imperial jurisdiction<ref name="Solo" /> during the years leading directly up to the [[Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Ferrix">{{Andor|Kassa (episode)}}</ref> Intended for use outside of the battlefield,<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" /> these walkers could traverse varied terrains including shallow waters<ref name="Solo" /> and volcanic mountains.<ref name="Dark Lord 23" /> The OI-CTs chassis consisted of large metal beams and two thick cables that met in the front to form a protruding crane boom and jib.<ref name="Solo" />

These walkers were commonly used for tasks such as moving [[Cargo container|shipping containers]] or picking up [[Starship|ships]] in [[salvage yard]]s, with operators specifically using these balanced frames to relocate unwieldly or heavy objects. Their four-legged design added stability and gave the operator room to brace and adjust the legs as needed in order to accommodate outsized loads.<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" />

==History==
[[File:OI-CT-Ahsoka.png|thumb|right|300px|Hera Syndulla observing an OI-CT at Santhe Shipyards]]
The OI-CT was manufactured by Kuat Drive Yards,<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" /> a corporation known for making a number of other influential walkers including the [[All Terrain Armored Transport]]<ref name="Facebook Walkers">{{Facebook|username=starwarsrebels|url=starwarsrebels/photos/a.230754950414469.1073741828.180356405454324/512572825566012|name=Star Wars Rebels|date=25-10-2015|quote=The iconic behemoth of the battlefield.|archivefile=File:AT-AT-Facebook.png}}</ref> and the [[All Terrain Scout Transport]]<ref name="Ultimate">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> They saw notable use on the [[planet]] [[Corellia]]<ref name="Solo" /> as early as [[13 BBY]]<ref name="TOG">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''</ref> and as late as [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Ahsoka Date">{{AhsokaSeriesDate}}</ref> traversing the shallow waters surrounding [[Coronet City]]'s [[Santhe Shipyards]].<ref name="Solo" /><ref name="Ahsoka"  /> They were also used on the planet [[Mustafar]] during the construction of [[Fortress Vader]]<ref name="Dark Lord 23" /> by [[12 BBY]].<ref name="Death note">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' states that [[Fortress Vader]] was completed forty-six [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Hosnian Cataclysm|Starkiller Incident]], which ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates to [[34 ABY]]. Therefore, the [[fortress]]'s construction, as well as the [[Battle of Fortress Vader]] that ensued, must have happened in [[12 BBY]].</ref>

Additionally, they were seen around [[Ferrix City]] on the planet [[Ferrix]]<ref name="Ferrix" /> as late as [[5 BBY]],<ref name="Andor Date">"That Would be me" takes place immediately after "[[Kassa (episode)|Kassa]]," which dates itself to [[5 BBY]].</ref> where they were used in conjunction with [[heavy industrial crane transport]]s by the local scrappers.<ref name="Ferrix" /> By 9 ABY,<ref name="Mando Date">{{MandoDate|19}}</ref> they were also utilized by the New Republic among the post-Imperial [[Shipyard Depot|salvage yards]] on [[Coruscant]], parked alongside dismantled [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer]]s when not in use during nighttime hours.<ref name="Mando" />

==Behind the scenes==
The OI-CT first appeared in the [[2018]] movie ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'',<ref name="Solo" /> but was not identified as such until [[2019]], in a video from the official "Star Wars Kids" YouTube channel.<ref name="YouTube" /> The concept was pitched by [[James Clyne]], design supervisor at [[Lucasfilm]],<ref name="ArtSolo">''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref> though concept artist [[Vincent Jenkins]] has also been credited with the walker's finalized appearance,<ref name="Instapost">{{Instagram|username=vincentjenkinsjnr|url=p/B1HNhdslmIu|name=[[Vincent Jenkins]]|date=2019-08-13|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/a0rH6}}</ref><ref name="Finalized Concept">{{ArtStation|username=vincentjenkins|url=artwork/k4m8zx|name=[[Vincent Jenkins]]|text=crane walker design for "solo"}}</ref> with further concepts from [[Thang Le]].<ref name="Thang Le">{{WebCite|url=https://thangle.com/portfolio-item/quick-tour|text=Thang Le - Quick Tour|work=[https://thangle.com/portfolio-item/quick-tour/ Thang Le Portfolio]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/WOhpq}}</ref>

[[File:OICT-ThangLe-ConceptArt.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Thang Le's OI-CT concept art mirroring real-world "Oakland cranes"]]
[[Pablo Hidalgo]] stated in a [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]] thread posted on [[April 11]], [[2023]], that the OI-CT calls back to a piece of real life folklore surrounding [[All Terrain Armored Transport|AT-ATs]] being inspired by [[Wikipedia:Oakland, California|Oakland]] [[Wikipedia:Crane (machine)|cranes]]. While he goes on to deny this claim,<ref name="Oakland">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1645921960696885248|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=The crane walker in this shot was a way to bring a piece of real world folklore full circle. If you live in the Bay Area, you'll hear the tale of how the AT-AT walkers were inspired by the Oakland cranes. It's not true. But, I named this walker design the OI-TC...|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/xxPyQ}}</ref> he goes on to facetiously reveal that he may have named the OI-CT either "Outsized Industrial Crane Transport" or "Oakland International Container Terminal."<ref name="Outsized">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1645922395319058432|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=... which is the Outsized Industrial Crane Transport... or maybe the Oakland International Container Terminal.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/CTCpW}}</ref> Hidalgo finished the thread by reaffirming the idea that James Clyne had major hand in the OI-CT's design, and that Clyne most definitely took inspiration from the aforementioned cranes, bringing the tale full circle.<ref name="Inspiration">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1645922804460843008|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=James Clyne designed the crane walker, in this case most definitely taking inspiration from the Oakland cranes. So now, when a cab driver in the Bay tells you that the cranes inspired a walker in Star Wars, it can be kinda true.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/4mNH9}}</ref>

The official reveal of the [[heavy industrial crane transport]] (HI-CT)'s name and acronym in a preview for the book [[2024]] ''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]'' lends credence to the notion that "Outsized Industrial Crane Transport" is, in fact, this walker's actual in-universe name.<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia" />
